The objectives are pursued with the support of the Internationalisation Service (SI) and the International Cooperation Development Sector (ISDN) , which act in accordance with the Commission for International Relations of the University. The activities are carried out, although within the framework of the competences of the respective Areas, in a framework of collaboration, exchange of information flows and integration, in close contact with the delegates for internationalisation of the Departments and Schools and with the International Relations Commission . With reference to the overall framework of funding, projects and actions foreseen by the Erasmus+ Community Programme, the competences are divided as follows: Erasmus+ Programme Actions Office KA 1: Learning mobility of individuals SI KA 2.1 Strategic Partnerships in education, training and youth SI KA 2.2 Knowledge Alliances SSCI KA 2.3 Sector Skills alliances SSCI KA 2.4 Capacity Building in the field of higher education SSCI KA 2.5 Capacity Building in the field of youth SSCI KA 3: Support for Policy Reform SSCI Jean Monnet SI The conclusion of bilateral cooperation agreements between the University of Genoa and higher education institutes of Member States and Partner Countries is desired by the Government bodies and promoted, in the manner described below, both by the core structures and by the two Support Services. The purpose of these agreements is to initiate cooperation for the carrying out of integrated teaching and scientific activities, for the development of integrated study programmes for students and for the implementation of joint cooperation projects promoted by the competent Community Agencies in the field of Higher Education and Culture. List of academic cooperation agreements by the Internationalisation Service (updated 04.08.2025) Procedure for stipulation In order to proceed with the stipulation of an academic cooperation agreement: the lecturer proposes to the Internationalisation Service ( relint@unige.it ) or to the International Cooperation Development Office ( intstrat@unige.it ) the academic cooperation agreement, accompanied by a synthetic project plan containing the main aims, the reasons for the choice of the partner(s) and, in the case of more than one partner, the specification of the role played by each the offices ascertain the legal status of the potential partner university and any variations to the standard UniGe agreement text made by it the proposing professor shares the final agreement text with the Delegate for International Relations of his/her Department, by sending an email in which the central office of reference ( relint@unige.it or intstrat@unige.it ) the office involved submits the proposal to the International Relations Commission, including the ascertainment of legal status and the observations regarding any variations in the text if the International Relations Commission accepts the proposal, the offices inform the proposing professor and proceed with the acquisition of the Rector's signature. Once signed, the agreement will be sent to the partner for countersignature. Once both parties have signed, the Delegate for International Relations, duly informed by the offices, shall inform the Department Council if the International Relations Commission expresses reservations regarding the proposal, the proposing professor shall be called upon to provide further clarifications in order to have more elements for evaluation. Italian version English version French version Spanish version Type of mobility implementation agreement The stipulation of an academic cooperation agreement may be preliminary or concomitant to the stipulation of an implementation mobility agreement focused on the exchange of teachers and/or students at University, School or Department level. The mobility implementation agreement may also be proposed outside an academic cooperation agreement, provided that it is supported by a solid project plan. It must, however, include the fundamental clauses (e.g.: safety, insurance). The objectives are pursued with the support of the Internationalisation Service (SI) and the International Cooperation Development Sector (ISDN) , which act in accordance with the Commission for International Relations of the University. The activities are carried out, although within the framework of the competences of the respective Areas, in a framework of collaboration, exchange of information flows and integration, in close contact with the delegates for internationalisation of the Departments and Schools and with the International Relations Commission . With reference to the overall framework of funding, projects and actions foreseen by the Erasmus+ Community Programme, the competences are divided as follows: Erasmus+ Programme Actions Office KA 1: Learning mobility of individuals SI KA 2.1 Strategic Partnerships in education, training and youth SI KA 2.2 Knowledge Alliances SSCI KA 2.3 Sector Skills alliances SSCI KA 2.4 Capacity Building in the field of higher education SSCI KA 2.5 Capacity Building in the field of youth SSCI KA 3: Support for Policy Reform SSCI Jean Monnet SI The conclusion of bilateral cooperation agreements between the University of Genoa and higher education institutes of Member States and Partner Countries is desired by the Government bodies and promoted, in the manner described below, both by the core structures and by the two Support Services. The purpose of these agreements is to initiate cooperation for the carrying out of integrated teaching and scientific activities, for the development of integrated study programmes for students and for the implementation of joint cooperation projects promoted by the competent Community Agencies in the field of Higher Education and Culture. List of academic cooperation agreements by the Internationalisation Service (updated 04.08.2025) Procedure for stipulation In order to proceed with the stipulation of an academic cooperation agreement: the lecturer proposes to the Internationalisation Service ( relint@unige.it ) or to the International Cooperation Development Office ( intstrat@unige.it ) the academic cooperation agreement, accompanied by a synthetic project plan containing the main aims, the reasons for the choice of the partner(s) and, in the case of more than one partner, the specification of the role played by each the offices ascertain the legal status of the potential partner university and any variations to the standard UniGe agreement text made by it the proposing professor shares the final agreement text with the Delegate for International Relations of his/her Department, by sending an email in which the central office of reference ( relint@unige.it or intstrat@unige.it ) the office involved submits the proposal to the International Relations Commission, including the ascertainment of legal status and the observations regarding any variations in the text if the International Relations Commission accepts the proposal, the offices inform the proposing professor and proceed with the acquisition of the Rector's signature. Once signed, the agreement will be sent to the partner for countersignature. Once both parties have signed, the Delegate for International Relations, duly informed by the offices, shall inform the Department Council if the International Relations Commission expresses reservations regarding the proposal, the proposing professor shall be called upon to provide further clarifications in order to have more elements for evaluation. Italian version English version French version Spanish version Type of mobility implementation agreement The stipulation of an academic cooperation agreement may be preliminary or concomitant to the stipulation of an implementation mobility agreement focused on the exchange of teachers and/or students at University, School or Department level. The mobility implementation agreement may also be proposed outside an academic cooperation agreement, provided that it is supported by a solid project plan. It must, however, include the fundamental clauses (e.g.: safety, insurance). These courses will take place in onrubrline mode; information on how to participate will be communicated from April 2026 by the Language Skills Development Department exclusively to the names selected on the basis of the indications received by the Welcome Office Department on 1 April 2026 and 28 May 2026; the lessons will take place between May and August 2026 . 2. AUTUMNAL COURSES 2026 These courses are reserved for aspiring international students who take the B2 Italian language test administered by TEST TE.L.E.MA.CO. on 14-15-16 September 2026 or the Italian language test administered by the Language Skills Development Sector on 17 September 2026 and have achieved an adequate score, even if lower than B2, established by the Language Skills Development Sector and which will be communicated shortly. IMPORTANT : those who take the Italian B2 test on the dates of the TE.L.E.MA.CO. test after the above-mentioned dates or the Italian B2 test on dates after 17 September will NOT be offered any Italian courses and will not be able to retake the test. The courses are differentiated according to the initial level of knowledge, which is verified by a test of knowledge of the Italian language Erasmus students are offered the pick-up service : you will be welcomed at the airport or at the station by colleagues of the student association GEG Gruppo Erasmus Genova who will accompany you to the hostel or to the university premises. Usa le tue credenziali UniGePASS e ottieni l'accesso ai servizi.
